subject: Opsify renewal: increase hosted API commit and surge protection
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@opsify.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: opsify-legal@opsify.com
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + request for higher monthly commit and burst handling

Hi Karthik,

Hope you had a good week. We're finalizing our Q2 roadmap and need to lock in changes to our Redwood Hosted API commitment for the renewal. Over the last quarter our production embedding and chat usage increased ~2.6x vs plan after rolling out the new recommendation feature. We expect sustained higher throughput and need: 

- Monthly commit increase from 3M tokens to 9M tokens (target start 2028-04-01)
- Burst tolerance for short spikes up to 250% of commit for 3-5 minute windows without hard 429s
- Clarify rate-limits per route (chat vs embeddings) and how graceful fallback to lower tier models would work

I've attached our Q1 usage export (Opsify_Q1_usage_report.csv) to show the traffic shape. We'd like to discuss pricing for a 12-month renewal with the higher commit and a short-term staging pool for canary traffic.

Can you propose a pathway and the procurement steps? Opsify legal is on cc — they'll want any contract/term changes and a PO template.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform
Opsify

---
Attachment: Opsify_Q1_usage_report.csv (text/csv)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@opsify.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for higher monthly commit and burst handling

Elena — thanks for the context and the usage dump, that makes the ask clear. High level proposal below (happy to iterate):

Option A — Annual commit + burst pocket (recommended)
- Monthly committed tokens: 9,000,000
- Burst pocket: additional 2,250,000 tokens/month (can be used within 3-5 minute windows; throttles smooth down after 5 minutes)
- Effective unit pricing: committed tier price (we'll include the table in the doc)
- Staging pool: 1 dedicated slot pool (0.5 GPU equivalent) for canary traffic at no extra commit for first 60 days

Option B — Phased ramp (lower initial commit)
- Start at 6,000,000 monthly commit, step to 9,000,000 after 90 days with usage triggers

Operational notes / next steps: 
- We can provision the burst cushion via a soft quota layer to avoid hard 429s; sustained >500% for >10 minutes will trigger auto-throttling or fallback to a compatible cheaper variant.
- Procurement: we need a signed PO or email confirmation from Opsify legal, and Redwood legal will prepare an amendment to the MSA reflecting commit changes and billing cadence.
- Please confirm if Opsify needs price hold for the full 12 months or prefers quarterly rate re-eval.

I'll loop in Marissa (Customer Success) on provisioning and Ben (Rev Ops) for billing/PO handling. If you can share the PO intent and any procurement timeline, I can get a contract amendment drafted today.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@opsify.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-15T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for higher monthly commit and burst handling

Thanks Elena — great to see the growth. A few ops items from our side so we can provision without surprises: 

- We can stand up the staging pool and a dedicated workload tag for Opsify; will need the service account names or IP allowlist for early access.
- For burst smoothing we use a token-based soft quota with an overage buffer; we'll open a runbook entry to measure how often you hit the 250% threshold during the first 30 days.
- Security/compliance: attaching a SOC2 snapshot for your review. If your security team needs additional artifacts (logs retention policy, KMS details), loop them in and we'll add a light artifact bundle.

Marissa (CS)
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: SOC2-snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Elena Rossi <elena@opsify.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: opsify-legal@opsify.com
Date: 2028-03-15T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for higher monthly commit and burst handling

Thanks Karthik / Marissa — we're aligned on the need for commit increase. Legal has reviewed and we are ready to issue a PO intent. Attached is our signed PO intent (Opsify_PO_intent_signed.pdf). A couple of clarifications before you draft the amendment: 

- Billing: We prefer monthly invoicing with net-30. Can you confirm there are no prorated charges for the staging pool in the first 60 days?
- Rate-limits: We want separate rate limits for embeddings (higher parallelism) and chat routes — can you include per-route QPS limits in the amendment?
- Fallback behavior: If you auto-fallback to a smaller model, will response latencies be signposted (header) and will you guarantee content consistency flags in the response?

If you can reply with an amendment draft and the pricing table, we'll escalate to procurement to sign the PO next week.

Elena

---
Attachment: Opsify_PO_intent_signed.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@opsify.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-16T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for higher monthly commit and burst handling

Elena — appreciate the fast turnaround and the PO intent. Per your asks below, please see the confirmed terms and the next steps: 

Summary of agreed commercial terms (will appear in amendment):
- Monthly committed tokens: 9,000,000 (billed monthly, net-30)
- Burst pocket: 2,250,000 tokens/month available as soft overage; overage beyond the pocket billed at 1.8x committed unit rate
- Staging pool: provisioned at no charge for first 60 days; after that, billed at 25% of committed unit price if retained
- Per-route soft QPS caps: embeddings: 600 QPS (soft), chat: 180 QPS (soft) — these are operational caps and will be enforced with graceful backpressure; we'll include exact header flags in the runbook for signaling fallbacks

Procurement and legal items: 
- I've attached the pricing table and a DocuSign amendment link: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/ABCD-OPSIFY-2028
- Redwood legal will add per-route QPS and header conventions to the amendment and include a paragraph describing fallback signaling and latency headers.
- Please countersign the DocuSign envelope and attach the signed PO to the HubSpot deal (link: https://app.redwood.com/hubspot/deal/OP-2028-114).

Operational handoff: Marissa will create a provisioning ticket and a 30/60/90 day measurement plan. We'll monitor the first 30 days for burst incidence and adjust the burst pocket if needed.

Next steps (simple):
1) Opsify signs DocuSign amendment and returns PO — ben to process billing setup.
2) Redwood provisions staging pool and tags traffic — marissa to schedule a 30-minute runbook walk-through.
3) Monitor & tweak: review usage at day 30 and confirm full rollout at day 60.

Thanks — I'll stay on the thread to close billing.

Best,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
